posts.summary: The mechanism end to end — the runaway, the cliff, and why the state it lands in cannot see itself.
Who is at risk: anxiety-proneness read as low damping, and the cheap test — tolerance, not settling time — that would settle it.
The rescue result: a cheap fixed floor beats an elaborate one — and re-checking your support is what destroys it.
A full rescue buys the recovered state nothing against the next trigger — the threshold restored is the threshold the next episode drains.
The same collapse run deliberately — Schein, Lifton, Stein — and the inversion: the same three guardrails, two of them flipped.
Why “the observer collapses reality” and “union with God” are one move — and how the frame steers the collapse to an owned destination.
The person at the top: leader and follower share one dissociation pointing opposite ways — the group as his externalized self.
The follower is a position, not a personality — seventy years of research tried to name the type and dissolved it instead. Expression is conditional; the instrument failed at .20.
Seven contemplative traditions, with no contact with each other, named this failure and prescribed the same five safeguards — primary-source passages.

What the traditions that survive the collapse wrote down — ethics first, metered pace, plural community, a teacher who points past himself, discernment as procedure — and why the clinical field is re-deriving the same list.
"Cult" is a category that does harm — to the people it is meant to protect — and the sources this series leans on helped justify kidnapping. Why it names mechanisms instead.
The levers without the mysticism: a masonic lodge and a false-bottomed suitcase run the same structure as the mystics — so the lever is a position, not a belief.
The unfalsifiable authority without a person: Horizon, Robodebt and the Dutch childcare affair — and the finding that measurement is not a safeguard, auditable measurement is.
The clinic in the model: the state is ambiguous by construction, the instruments false-positive, and the honest measure is impairment, duration — and a holder.
The state cannot initiate its own exit: an outside relationship is necessary, a verdict is the harm — deprogramming, exit counselling, and the in-between time.
The Western esoteric tradition ran the same induction, named the same failure and built the same safeguards into a syllabus — and published its own predation account.
The case studies, opening: one mechanism in four environments — and the finding that the environment sets the price, not whether the move is used.
The method: what a predator never has to build, because the surrounding culture already built it — an inventory of pre-supplied levers.
Hidden agency: a cosmology in which harm is real but invisible and suffering is a debt — the unfalsifiable slot, pre-supplied.
Ranked inner state: enlightenment as a hierarchy nobody can check — and why wanting the next rung is obedience.
The state itself: where dissociation is already holy, the damage arrives pre-legitimised and the alarm is off.
The destination: a host culture certifies the teacher before he arrives — and the check on him reads as bigotry.
The same mechanism outside Brazil: a guru who taught emptying the self and being filled with him — in a tradition that had already named the state and called it not the goal.
An environment that supplies nothing: post-Soviet Ukraine, the vacuum, and the group that filled it — the same mechanism as Brazil and Japan, at a different price.
The one case where the group did not find a dissociation but designed one: a technique written to produce the state on schedule, then read as the goal.
The same manufactured collapse with no mysticism at all: est and the Landmark Forum — fatigue, confrontation, the state, and the appraisal sold as “Transformation.”
The mechanism's third route: the same state appraised as breakthrough or bad trip — and “set and setting” is the frame lever, named by the field as a risk factor.
A first-person account: a practitioner describes the environment that supplies the frame, reports being recruited and getting out — and contradicts this series where it matters most.
One scale up: what a culture takes reality to be is a frame like any other — it supplies a reading, it can be checked or not, and someone benefits from the naming.
Why a materialist cosmology cannot measure the collapse: no category means misfiling, not absence — and an unfilled category is a vacancy a coercive frame can occupy.
The living cosmos has a reading for the collapse — and that is its danger: the safeguard is structural, a plane of many participants and a practitioner who does not stand above it.
The third possibility: a frame with a reading, a purpose, and a seat — the cosmological form of every case study, and why the traditions refused to name the endpoint.
Apophatic cosmology: a correspondence with no endpoint — the architectural countermeasure to the seat, and, because it can be claimed, not self-enforcing.
Witzel's deep-mythology finding as the fourth convergence: the frames a person is inside were inherited tens of millennia ago — and the oldest disagreement is about whether reality has an endpoint.

A close reading of Frater Acher's Holy Daimon: systasis as a meeting between two parties, a guide that is unowned, and a practice whose stated direction runs outward — and the one safeguard the book never writes down.

The one-to-one case of the levers-as-positions: an operator reads a person's own frame, finds the position it already leaves open and occupies it — so the target's frame does the installing, and it cannot be reported from inside.
A close reading of Frater Acher's Holy Heretics — the apophatic path of unknowing as a practice, and the book's own charge that organised orthodoxy, not unauthorised experience, is the poison.

A close reading of Paul Levy's Undreaming Wetiko — the collapse named as a contagion, a cosmology with no intrinsic existence that can still kill, and a cure that is the blog's own boundary: labelling the possessed is itself the virus.
A close reading of Jung's Memories, Dreams, Reflections — the confrontation with the unconscious as a controlled descent, held by a task and a myth the book then says we no longer have.
A close reading of Gordon White's Ani.Mystic — a cosmology of a living, animated cosmos, read as a frame held and examined rather than adopted.
A close reading of Gordon White's Star.Ships — the deep-prehistory argument that the spirits came first, read at its own scale and against the blog's inherited-frame finding.
A close reading of Adams & Poncet's Two Esoteric Tarots — a frame built by named people with a claimed lineage, and the authority over what the cards 'are' as a dispute auditable from outside.

What an operator does when the fit is refused: recode the rejection as the target's symptom, pivot to the surrounding support structures, and make the target's own accurate report do the discrediting.

A close reading of Mark Stavish's Egregores — the entity the blog used for its predation account, read whole: a group-made mind that is normatively neutral, and the deprogramming chapter the blog never cited.

A close reading of Zimbardo's The Lucifer Effect — the situational thesis at book length, and the certified frame whose record has since collapsed: what the archive shows the Stanford Prison Experiment actually was.

A close reading of Lifton's Thought Reform and the Psychology of Totalism — the eight criteria the blog has run all along on secondary summaries, read at source, and the certified checklist they became.
A close reading of Arendt's Eichmann in Jerusalem — the banality of evil at source, used by the blog through Zimbardo and never read, and the phrase's own contested history.
A close reading of Fromm's The Anatomy of Human Destructiveness — the necrophilous character as a structure, and the biophilia that answers it.
A close reading of Stratton-Kent's Geosophia — the underworld tradition read as the practice the blog's Western column lacks.
A close reading of the Quareia curriculum whole — the practice the blog has been quoting in modules, read end to end.
A close reading of Acher's Black Abbot White Magic — Trithemius's angelic magic and the Steganographia read as a frame hidden in plain sight, and the third Acher book.
The position nobody defended: authority taken by assumption rather than claim, and the provocation calibrated so that a challenger's reaction becomes the evidence against them.
A close reading of Greer's The Blood of the Earth — magic and peak oil, a collapse with no holder, and the industrial frame that cannot imagine its own end.
A close reading of the Picatrix — the operable cosmology at source: a world where everything corresponds, and a grimoire that states the seat without ever arguing for it.
A close reading of the Chaldean Oracles — the theurgic root of the whole Western lineage: fire, the flower of mind, and a seat that is a cosmos rather than a person.
A close reading of the Orphic Hymns — a frame enacted rather than argued: no doctrine, no thesis, and a cosmos named into presence by invocation.

posts.summary: A close reading of Proclus’ Theology of Plato in Thomas Taylor’s translation — the frame that argues, in a hierarchy of mediation, for a cosmos with an explicit claim on how things are.
